To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity to load mismatch is amplifier architecture and predistortion model dependent and that the adaptive DPD models are more robust to load mismatch.

the linearity degration in the power amplifiers studied is significant and that adaptive DPD schemes using the GMP and KV models can mitigate the linearity degrading effects of load impedance mismatches.

1) The sensitivity to load impedance mismatches varies depending on the amplifier architecture, 2) The MLP model is not able to compensate for the load impedance mismatch in the studied adaptive scheme, and 3) The GMP and KV models are able to compensate for load impedance mismatches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a thorough analysis of the effects of the load impedance mismatch on the performance of digitally predistorted power amplifiers.
the effects of load mismatch on the linearity performance of digitally predistorted power amplifiers, which is a key aspect in the design of future wireless transmitters.
the sensitivity of linearized power amplifiers to load impedance mismatch and how this mismatch can be compensated for by using an adaptive DPD model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the GMP model is the most suitable model to tackle load mismatch conditions, while KV model is the most robust model to tackle load impedance mismatch in adaptive schemes, and the MLP model should be avoided in adaptive schemes.
the GMP and KV models outperform the MLP model in terms of load impedance mismatch sensitivity and in adaptive DPD schemes.
, in the adaptive DPD scheme with a GMP model, the linearity degrades by less than 1.5 dB in the in-band distortions and by 3.5 dB in out-of-band distortons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GMP and KV models are more robust against load impedance mismatch and they are also more efficient in terms of memory requirements than MLP.
the GMP model is the best candidate for adaptive DPD schemes when load impedance mismatch is a concern.
adaptive DPD schemes using GMP or KV models are able to compensate for the effects of load impedances mismatch in the linearity of the power amplifier.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in adaptive DPD schemes for linearized power amplifiers, it is necessary to consider a memory model for the nonlinear behavior of the PA, in order to achieve a robust performance in presence of load impedance mismatch.

the DPD model structure has a strong impact on the linearity performance of the linearized amplifier when load impedance mismatch is present, and the GMP and KV structures are more effective than the MLP structure in this scenario.
the sensitivity of the power amplifier linearity to load impedance mismatch can be reduced by the use of adaptive digital predistortion techniques.
